children: Chicago soybeans and corn lost more ground on Friday, as rapid US harvesting and positioning ahead of key global supply-demand reports weighed on prices.
Wheat rose for the first time in three sessions as disruptions to Black Sea exports underpinned the market.
* The most-active soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT)
fell 0.1% to $12.86-1/2 a bushel by 0006 GMT and corn
* Grain traders are tracking corn and soybean harvest progress in near-perfect weather in the US Midwest, while awaiting monthly US Department of Agriculture reports due later in the day.
* The USDA is expected to lower its average corn yield estimate but increase its end-of-season US supply view, according to analysts polled by Reuters.

* The agency is due to update its corn and soybean crop progress estimates on Monday and traders expect a sharp increase in harvesting as clear weather allowed Midwest farmers to resume field work after rain delays at the end of last month.
* The wheat market was supported by a lack of supplies from Russia and Ukraine. Traders have been monitoring news from the Black Sea region as the two countries seek alternative export routes.
* Export capacity at Russia's Baltic Sea ports has increased. Ukraine is seeking to ship grain via the Baltic Sea as well as German ports.

* Global shares slid on Thursday as a mild pullback in sovereign bond yields was countered by a jump in oil prices and indicators of the massive debt that technology companies may need to sustain their dramatic artificial intelligence-fuelled growth.
